articles.body:
Wine Wars: Coronata is one of two subquests in the Wine Wars questline in The Witcher 3's second expansion, Blood and Wine , to resolve the rival vineyards' issues.

You will start this quest automatically if you agree to help Liam de Coronata during Wine Wars: Belgaard at Plegmund's Bridge.

How to Complete All Wine Wars: Coronata Activities

To complete Wine Wars: Coronata, you must resolve the following five tasks in the area surrounding the Coronata vineyard:

1. Vineyard Infestation (Archespores) located in the fields north of Coronata Vineyard, northeast of Plegmund's Bridge. Destroy the monster nest to complete the objective.

2. Guarded Treasure (Archespores) located in the clearing south of the Trading Post, northeast of Coronata Vineyard. Kill all the archespores.

3. Abandoned Site (Archespores) located in the woods to the southeast of Coronata Vineyard, northeast of Dulcinea Windmill. Defeat the lone archespore to reclaim the site.

4. Hidden Treasure (Rabid rock trolls) located at the Pittapatte River Crossing, a small bridge over the river southeast of the Trading Post, northeast of Dun Tynne Castle. After killing them, check the corpse at the east end of the bridge to find the "Letter to Cosmo Cyrille" and a key to a lockbox. Reading the letter begins the Treasure Hunt Coin Doesn't Stink .

5. Person in Distress (Bandits) located in the woods northeast of the Trading Post. There is a cave entrance in a ravine northeast of the marker. Inside are three bandits holding the Coronata herbalist hostage. Slaying the bandits starts a scene with the herbalist where you can either travel with them to Coronata Vineyard (near where you can finish Coin Doesn't Stink ) or stay in the cave to loot the area.

Choices you made earlier, and what you do now, affect what happens next.

Once you've completed these five tasks, you have three options. You can either:

Return to the clerk at Plegmund's Bridge to explain that you've resolved Coronata's problems, letting him acquire Belgaard.

If you wait to turn this quest in, then you can also complete Wine Wars: Vermentino .

If you acquire both hidden notes during this quest and Vermentino's, then you can unlock Wine Wars: The Deus in the Machina . This is the best ending to this questline, since you find out what's really going on, and you maximize your rewards.

No matter what option you pick, you will get the same reward - at least 525 Crowns or up to 875 Crowns if you haggled - just at different stages based on when you turn it in.

articles.body:
Wine Wars: The Deus in the Machina is a secret bonus quest in the Wine Wars side story from The Witcher 3 's second expansion, Blood and Wine . In it, you uncover the full story of what's going on with the vineyards.

To unlock The Deus in the Machina, you must:

Find the Orders on Elegant Stationery at the Hidden Treasure northeast of the Coronata vineyard during Wine Wars: Coronata .

Find the Letter on Elegant Stationery and Heavy Brass Key at the Hidden Treasure north of Corvo Bianco during Wine Wars: Vermentino .

Once you've found and read both clues from their respective quests, Geralt will comment on them, and you'll unlock The Deus in the Machina. Your first task is to find the place mentioned in the letter, which is located in the south of Beauclair, directly east of Tesham Mutna Ruins and southwest of Trastamara Hunting Cottage.

You can visit the Ducal Clerk at Plegmund's Bridge to suggest possible sabotage at both vineyards but there is no reward for doing so.

When you arrive at the location, you'll find a small building. Go down to the lower grassy part in the center of the area to find the door to a warehouse tucked between shrubs - it's similar to how the wine cellar at Corvo Blanco is situated.

Enter the warehouse, and you will find one archespore to deal with (remember they're weak to Igni). After it is down, use Witcher Senses to search the area.

So long as you have not completed Wine Wars: Coronata or Vermentino yet, you can properly investigate the warehouse. Start by locating the archespore plants against the right wall, which you can optionally destroy by burning them with Igni. This will give you +100 XP.

Then, investigate the crate against the back wall and read the Stocktaking Report. On reading the report, you learn that Count Crespi, Belgaard’s erstwhile owner, is behind the archespore sabotage.

The quest updates, instructing you to notify Liam and Matilda at Plegmund’s Bridge and tell them you know the saboteur’s identity.

Going back to Plegmund's Bridge and reporting your findings ends Wine Wars: Coronata, Vermentino, and The Deus in the Machina (receive an additional 250 XP) quests, regardless of how many objectives you have completed for the first two.

However, if you had unfinished tasks relating to either vineyard, then you will unlock the Wine Wars: Consorting quest , which simply collates the outstanding objectives for you to complete. Since Coronata and Vermentino have now joined forces, it’s both sides’ five tasks bundled into one larger quest, but the tasks remain the same.

articles.title: Village of Lu Memory Flower Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: As you travel around the Village of Lu, you'll want to stop and grab these Memory Flowers as you go by. These flowers are the only way to increase your
articles.body:
As you travel around the Village of Lu, you'll want to stop and grab these Memory Flowers as you go by. These flowers are the only way to increase your overall health pool in Phantom Blade 0, so you don't want to miss them. Below you'll find all of the Memory Flowers for the Village of Lu map.

Found to the right of the Mandate Encampment Outer Gate Bell. You'll see it if you follow the path up to the Mandate Gate on the east side of the Village of Lu

Found immediately after defeating Zhou Bi, The Gatekeeper. To the left of the arena, you'll see the memory flower through the small gateway. Two children will be looking at the flower.

From the Covered Bridge Bell, go through the gateway to its right. Follow the path down and around through the building and the field with the scarecrow. You'll find the next Memory Flower at an altar with about 5 enemies praying to it. It will also be marked with a Purple Icon on your map for the Secrets at the Heart of the Lake quest

Upon crossing the Covered Bridge, follow the path until you can fork right. A large lady enemy will be blocking the doorway to a house. Defeat her and go down the ladder found inside the house. A hole in the wall will lead outside, where you'll find the next Memory Flower on the ridge.

Upon defeating Master Bi Yuan of the Tianxuan Sect, you'll find a newly sprouted Memory Flower in the arena

After picking up Memory Flower 5, turn around and head toward the small stairs leading up to the house across the way. Head inside and make a left. The next Memory Flower will be in the room.

After defeating Master Bi, Hai of Kuye Temple, you'll find the next Memory Flower in the middle of the battle arena

After grabbing Memory Flower 7 head upstream toward the purple glowing chest containing a Blackstone Fragment in it. Continue past the chest until you reach the end of the river, here you'll find a few enemies and another Memory Flower.

From the Terraces Bell head into the house on your right. Inside, you'll find Memory Flower 9 sitting on a table.

Upon reaching the Engine Giant Remains Bell, head inside the shrine and attack the human body that is impaling the spear into the giant monster. After the body is destroyed Memory Flower 10 will be in its place.

After grabbing Memory Flower 10 drop down the hole in front of you. Follow the dirt road path to the left hopping over the fallen tree. You'll see the next Memory Flower slightly to your right at the end of the path.

Upon leaving the Survivors Courtyard Bell head left and go down the stairs. You'll see the next Memory Flower on a small wooden workbench next to a giant hole

Memory Flower 13 is found at the Temple of Blue Fireflies Bell, which isn't accessible until players have reached the Survivors Courtyard Bell and made their way down from the north side of the map. Inside the Shrine, you'll find the Memory Flower on the altar.

Leave the Temple of Blue Fireflies and make your way back toward the Well of the Three Puppets in the center of the village. You'll come across a stone bridge that connects the two locations. On the right-hand side of the bridge, you'll find the next Memory Flower down below in the river.

Once you drop down the Well of The Three Puppets after successfully clearing out the threads, you'll find the next Memory Flower as soon as you load back in.

Those are all of the Memory Flowers for the Village of Lu. As you're going through the area, be sure to check out our main walkthrough so you don't miss a beat while exploring the map

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero November 3 Patch Notes - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The November 3, 2026 Patch for Phantom Blade Zero has arrived, bringing with it a number of general optimizations and adjustments to improve game performance,
articles.body:
The November 3, 2026 Patch for Phantom Blade Zero has arrived, bringing with it a number of general optimizations and adjustments to improve game performance, balance, and overall stability.

This page acts as a comprehensive breakdown of the November 3 Patch for Phantom Blade Zero, including a link to the full Patch Notes.

Added “Hit Sound Intensity” and “Hit Impact Sound Intensity” options to the audio settings.

[PC] Added support for remapping “Interact / Talk” for both keyboard and controller.

Adjusted the combat behavior of certain bosses and enemies, along with the functionality of certain environmental mechanisms.

Reduced the frequency of grab attacks used by Hua, Deadly Betrothed on Wayfarer and Pathbreaker difficulties. Other difficulty settings are unaffected.

Improved weapon hit feedback and adjusted the volume of certain sound effects and dialogue.

Updated weapon descriptions, certain skill descriptions, and controller button icons.

[PC] Updated the shader compilation process to significantly reduce startup times. Ray tracing shaders will no longer be compiled by default at startup. Players who previously had Ray Tracing disabled will need to recompile shaders on their first launch after installing this patch. This is a one-time process and should take only a short time. Players who previously had Ray Tracing enabled can start playing without recompiling shaders. If you enable Ray Tracing in the settings, the required ray tracing shaders will be compiled separately the next time you restart the game.

[PC] Reduced stuttering that could occur when using a controller connected via Bluetooth.

[PC] NVIDIA Reflex now works when set to “Auto” with V-Sync enabled.

Fixed issues that could prevent progression under certain conditions.● Fixed environmental issues that could cause the player character to become stuck.

Fixed various issues with cutscenes and visuals.● Fixed several combat-related issues.

Fixed an issue that caused character hair to render incorrectly on certain AMD graphics cards with specific driver versions. We will continue to monitor your feedback and improve the game experience. To report an issue or share your feedback, please visit our official support page . Please note the following common issues related to this update:

Some third-party mods are not compatible with this update and may cause issues. If you encounter problems after updating, please remove any installed mods.

If you experience crashes or stuttering after updating, please clear the game’s shader cache and relaunch the game. Shaders will then be quickly recompiled. Cache file location: right-click Phantom Blade Zero in your Steam Library, select Manage → Browse local files, then go to the PBZ\ProjectPBZ\Saved\Cache folder and delete the files inside.

If you wish to read the Patch Notes in full, you can do so via the official Steam news post .

articles.title: Pilot Draws Incredible GTA 6 Mural With His Flight Path
articles.summary: Benjamin McDaniel, who calls himself The Pilot Picasso, just unveiled his new masterpiece: a GTA 6 mural drawn by flying his plane. Using flight path visualization systems, you can watch his entire journey and see the artwork come to life.
articles.body:
Benjamin McDaniel, who calls himself The Pilot Picasso, just unveiled his new masterpiece: a GTA 6 mural drawn by flying his plane. Using flight path visualization systems, you can watch his entire journey and see the artwork come to life.

It’s kind of like an Etch A Sketch because it’s a continuous line from start to finish, which is part of what makes the feat so impressive. The other thing that makes it impressive is, you know, he kept the plane in the sky the entire time.

He took off from Bentonville (QTV) airstrip at 11.29am and landed back at the same airport at 19:37pm. It took him eight hours and eight minutes to complete the piece, which he traced in the sky with a Cessna Skylane RG. The feat was completed on November 5 and you can check it out on FlightRadar24 . Here’s a tweet showcasing the finished thing:

The turns to make the alligator were the most fun to watch. Well done @thepilotpicasso. — Flightradar24 (@flightradar24) November 6, 2026

The turns to make the alligator were the most fun to watch. Well done @thepilotpicasso.

The artwork showed the GTA 6 logo next to an alligator, palm trees, a sports car, and a bikini clad woman. A helicopter hovered above the logo.

His upcoming projects include a classical piece and a Thanksgiving piece. In a recent interview, he said , “Safety is number one. If bad weather rolls around, I push the flight to another day or another week.”

In October, The Pilot Picasso flew a route that traced out the Mona Lisa , and previously he also flew Edvard Munch’s The Scream . Previous pop culture artworks include The Lord of The Rings , Skyrim , and Spider-Man .

Analysts expect GTA 6 will make over $5 billion in launch week alone , so expect it to fill your feeds for a few weeks. GTA 6 is scheduled to be released on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

articles.title: Nier: Automata Dev Working on Fix for Patch That Accidentally Bloated the Game Size to 366GB on PC
articles.summary: Nier: Automata got a patch yesterday to add support for more languages to the game (Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), but it accidentally bloated the game file size to 366GB on PC. That’s 1.5 copies of GTA 6!
articles.body:
Nier: Automata got a patch yesterday to add support for more languages to the game (Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), but it accidentally bloated the game file size to 366GB on PC. That’s 1.5 copies of GTA 6 !

A bug caused the entire game to be applied to every DLC pack included in the PC edition, ballooning the overall file size to Call of Duty-esque heights. Nier was previously around 50GB to download.

The game saw a wave of negative reviews come in on Steam following the patch, with players complaining that they were unable to play or, you know, download any other games.

"Claude, please add new language support for my game, no mistakes, masterpiece. It's 366 gigabytes now? Splendid,” said one review, making a joke about Square Enix using AI. “Undeniably good game which I've had to remove from my computer because some genius, presumably misusing automated tools, packed it into itself six times over, making a 360 gig install file. I'll recommend this game after it is fixed,” said another.

“I think the funniest part about the ‘slight’ issue with the new update for language support is the Steam page still lists a 50gb storage requirement. Good one guys,” reads another negative review. “Played this on PS4 loved it but 366GB is unacceptable for a company like them... fix this Square or I will STOP my FF14 sub,” read another.

Square Enix has offered a workaround for the Nier: Automata issue as it works on a fix. “We have confirmed an issue where, following the latest update to the Steam version of Nier: Automata, the installation process indicates that more storage space is required than expected,” the company said in a Japanese tweet .

“We are currently investigating the cause and working on a solution. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game by unchecking the DLC under Steam → Properties → DLC.”

Of course, Nier fans are desperate for a proper follow-up to Nier: Automata, but so far nothing has been announced. In November last year, Yoko Taro said he’d been working on various projects , but they just keep getting canceled. “I often get told stuff like, ‘Why aren’t you making a new sequel to NieR?’ or, ‘Yoko Taro isn’t doing anything,’ but that’s because recently, a lot of projects I was involved in got discontinued midway through development," he said.

"I’ve actually been working on some stuff, it’s just that it never ended up seeing the light of day. I got paid for it, so I personally have no issues with that, but people seem to think that I haven’t been doing anything just because none of the work I’ve done is being released."

articles.title: Nintendo Exec Bill Trinen Explains Why the Ocarina of Time Remake Is the Perfect First The Legend of Zelda Game
articles.summary: Nintendo of America Vice President of Player & Product Experience Bill Trinen has seen a lot of Zelda games in his nearly 30-year career at the company. He got his start translating bug reports on the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the N64 in the '90s. And with the newly released and critically acclaimed remake, he acknowledged that, internally, there's always a bit of a different buzz when working on a new Zelda game.
articles.body:
Nintendo of America Vice President of Player & Product Experience Bill Trinen has seen a lot of Zelda games in his nearly 30-year career at the company. He got his start translating bug reports on the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the N64 in the '90s. And with the newly released and critically acclaimed remake, he acknowledged that, internally, there's always a bit of a different buzz when working on a new Zelda game.

"Zelda games always come kind of with their own unique energy," he told me at the launch event for the Ocarina of Time Remake at the Nintendo Store in San Francisco. "This moment in particular, I think, is big for all of them [internally], both just because, like, we've talked about how much the game meant to a lot of people back then, but also the role that it plays within the overall Zelda 40th anniversary."

The original Legend of Zelda was released for the NES in 1986. Ocarina of Time, in 1998, was the first 3D Zelda game, something that Trinen said this remake release brings back memories of. "The [1998] game itself was just so foundational for [this] kind of 3D adventure game, as a whole, and it just was this moment in time where it was like, everybody was on this journey together."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Launch Photos

Ocarina of Time has stood the test of time in being regarded as one of the greatest games of all time, but not everyone has played it , whether it was because they didn't have an N64 back then, or that they weren't born yet. Trinen has a message for those players: "This is the perfect place for your first Zelda game, because you are gonna learn everything that there is about the world and the characters that will serve sort of as the foundation for all the others, all the games that came after," he said.

"This game is sort of a really foundational story for the lore of the Legend of Zelda. It really tells the story of Link and his journey becoming a hero. It tells the story of Link and his connection to Zelda and their relationship with Ganondorf. And overall, it communicates kind of what is at the moral core of is all the series, which is the idea that wisdom and courage combined can overcome power."

Trinen also shared his favorite moment from Ocarina of Time [SPOILER WARNING] .

"I have to say my favorite moment in Ocarina is the moment when Link leaves Kokiri Forest for the first time. It's an emotional moment. You say goodbye to a friend. There's a tinge of sadness to it, and then the whole world opens up before you, and you just see Hyrule Fields spread out. And all the possibility and exploration and discovery that awaits, you just sort of see across the field in the list, and you start to wonder, 'Okay, what am I gonna do next?' So it's sort of this really magical moment of almost, you know, leaving your childhood for the first time and setting out into the world, that happens early in the game, and it's a really special part of Link's overall journey."

Finally, when I put Trinen on the spot to ask him his favorite Zelda game of all time, he said it's changed over time and answered with a big smile on his face. "Oh, you know, it changes with time. You know, there were points where it was Majora's Mask, and points where it was Wind Waker, or Breath of the Wild. I would say, the role that Ocarina of Time played both in terms of the impact on Nintendo, the impact on the games industry, the impact it had for the series overall, that makes it such a core experience that the Nintendo Switch 2 version is my current new favorite."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is out now exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2. You can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time Remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas , and Early Item Bag Expansions . If you’re looking for more, don’t miss our complete guides to All Pieces of Heart , All Gold Skulltulas , and All Empty Bottles !

articles.body:
For the next two weeks, US retailer Best Buy is hosting a slew of "early Black Friday deals" in the run-up to its proper Black Friday sale that starts on November 19. From November 6, those looking to get some of their holiday shopping done early can sift through the retailer's early discounts, which include a rotation of "Doorbuster" deals that will, supposedly, have you rushing to make a purchase.

Dramatic, I know, but let's take a look at what's on sale, and what's worth picking up now, rather than simply waiting until the sales get even better at the end of the month.

We've already seen a few decent discounts as part of the DoorBOOsters sale over Halloween (October 30-November 1), but now we're getting into the real meat and potatoes of the holiday sale season.

November 6 - November 19 : Early Black Friday Deals + Doorbusters

November 19 - 28 : Black Friday Doorbusters + Deals

November 29 - 30 : Cyber Monday Sale Event

December 18 - 24 : Last-Minute Savings Event

It tells you when the biggest upcoming games are coming out and has all the gaming deals in one place.

articles.body:
A big feature in the Crimson Desert DLC, Charting the Unknown, is getting your own ship to sail the Pywel seas. If you're wondering how to get your first ship, how to get better ones, and other useful info like how to upgrade your ship, you're in the right place. Depending on where you are in the story, it can be confusing since it isn't quite clear!

How to Get Your First Ship in Charting the Unknown

Before you go looking for a ship, make sure you have the Charting the Unknown DLC. Sailing isn't part of the base game; therefore, you won't be able to do it without the DLC. Once you have it, you'll need to have progressed far enough in the Greymanes Faction Quests .

As explained in our overall DLC guide , you'll need to complete the Gathered Will quest chain under Grounds of the Sunrise . This requires finishing the final quest in that quest chain, Expanding the Camp . After doing so, you should have access to the new Greymanes Faction Quest category, Charting the Unknown.

You can then follow the quest chain for A Wider World to build your first ship. This will also introduce how sailing works, pioneering an island, and more.

Once you've gotten your first ship, the Small Greymane Ship, you may want to get a bigger one. This is a good way to sail faster, carry more trade goods, and boost your firepower. However, you'll need a whole lot of Camp Funds and/or materials before you can get a new one.

There are many basic ships that you can buy by simply going to the right port. We've included some basic information on how much they cost and where to find them in the table below. While each ship size runs for the same cost, they do have different stats. And if you want a legendary ship, you'll need to track down the right blueprints before you can build it.

How to Upgrade a Ship in Charting the Unknown

Before you can upgrade a ship in Crimson Desert, you'll need to get upgrades to equip. And on top of that, many ship parts are specific to the ship's size. You can either buy ship parts from a Ship Outfitter , found at certain ports, or craft them yourself. One location to find a Ship Outfitter is the Silvermoon Tradehouse/Demeniss Port.

But if you've found a blueprint that you'd like to craft, you'll need a Workstation. You can place a Sturdy Workstation at your house or use one at a facility like the Timberham Sawmill after getting it up and running . Once you want to equip those new parts to your ship, find a Ship Manager at a port. Speak to them via the Manage Ships prompt and then if your ship is in port, tap Manage Ships next.

Hover over the ship that you want to customize and press the Change Equipment button prompt visible along the bottom of your screen. This will reveal a new window where you can equip ship parts from your inventory. With that said, certain slots will be locked if your ship isn't large enough.

articles.title: Rockstar Will Be Keen to Release GTA 6 on PC Sooner Rather Than Later Because of AI Clones, Former Dev Says
articles.summary: Rockstar may officially release GTA 6 on PC soon after console over concern about AI-generated clones, one former developer has said.
articles.body:
Rockstar may officially release GTA 6 on PC soon after console over concern about AI-generated clones, one former developer has said.

In an interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible, due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.

People are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. We've seen everything from Minecraft playable on X/Twitter to modders shoving Minecraft and Elden Ring together . Indeed, last month, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline.

Seemingly in response, Anthropic issued an update for Claude that made it harder for people to use the AI model to generate video game clones, but concern that GTA 6 could pop up on PC soon after it hits PlayStation and Xbox remains.

There is also concern around the security of the PS5, with Sony seemingly engaged in a game of Whac-a-Mole with hackers who are trying to jailbreak the latest firmware ahead of the release of GTA 6. This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6 to run, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.

"[Generative AI] really has changed the world," Vermeij said, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking.

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest. I don't see it. But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job.

“But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years how that's going to pan out."

In October, GamesBeat reported that Rockstar was indeed planning to release GTA 6 on PC during the first quarter of 2027. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two did not comment on the report.

If true, it would mean GTA 6 hitting PC just a few months after it launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Some had anticipated a longer wait for the game on PC, given it took nearly two years for GTA 5 to launch on PC after consoles.

The PC launch may tie into the release of GTA 6's multiplayer mode, which fans are calling GTA Online 2 while they wait for official word from Rockstar. While Rockstar has yet to confirm an online mode for GTA 6, last month Twitch boss Dan Clancy said GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — will launch next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has always responded with vague comments when asked about the prospect of launching GTA 6 on PC, pointing to Rockstar for announcements. In May, Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that you're judged by serving the core. Like really serving the core consumer. If your core consumer isn't there, if they're not served first and best, you kind of don't hit your other consumers.”

Red Dead Redemption, GTA 5, LA Noire, Max Payne 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2 all came to PC after consoles. And while GTA's core audience may be on console, it has a huge fanbase of active players on PC, fueled by GTA Online and role-play servers.

Analysts expect GTA 6 will make over $5 billion in launch week alone . GTA 6 is scheduled to be released on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: How Remedy designed Control Resonant’s wildest mission: ‘Anything kind of goes’
articles.summary: Time-travel stories are illogical’ by nature. But for Resonant’s version to work, Remedy had to make the physical space a lot easier to follow.
articles.body: Note: Some spoilers for Control Resonant’s “Recursions and Iterations” mission follow. One of Control Resonant’s most memorable missions involves time travel — kind of. There are certainly multiple timelines intersecting, or maybe overlapping, or maybe running in parallel. As protagonist Dylan Faden, you meet some of the researchers who are trapped in and investigating these timeline anomalies. Dylan’s first encounter with the researchers is somehow not the researchers’ first time meeting Dylan. But before we can learn much more, time glitches out, and they all turn up dead. That seems to be the end result in every timeline Dylan comes across, even toward the end of the mission. What does it all mean for this timeline, the one we’re playing? Did the act of tracking down the researchers change our timeline? Are we in a different timeline entirely? I wasn’t sure what to make of it when I finished the mission, and I’m not alone — even the developers at Remedy had trouble keeping track of it all. “I don’t actually remember where we landed on with the writing,” says lead level designer Anne-Marie Grönroos, turning the question over to senior level designer Admir Burnic. “Like, are the researchers even there after the mission is done? Are they still living their life?” [Image: Burnic isn’t sure, and I tell them I’m not entirely sure, either. But that’s not really the point of the mission. Like many of Remedy’s best sequences, the “Recursions and Iterations” mission is more about the unease of knowing something is wrong but not exactly what it is, the subtle horror of realizing generally what’s been happening but not necessarily why. Maybe the narrative team did establish a canon ending for the researchers and all three of us just missed it, or maybe it was ambiguous on purpose. “It’s funny, when you’re dealing with this sort of time-travel stuff, timelines, whatever, there’s always this aspect to it where it’s almost illogical,” Burnic says. “So anything kind of goes. I mean, it could be intentional. It could also not be intentional.” --- Prepare for (being inspired by) Titanfall. Toward the end of “Recursions and Iterations,” there’s a mind-bending combat sequence in which a bunch of Dylans, presumably from the other timelines, glitch in to join the fight. Burnic says this was a somewhat late addition inspired by “Effect and Cause,” a mission from Titanfall 2. > There’s this time-travel mission in Titanfall 2. I was really inspired by that. I wanted to do something along those lines, but I was looking for “What’s the Remedy version of it?” And at some point I had this idea of glitches of Dylan showing up executing enemies. I remember it was fairly late in production, so it was a bit risky. I knew I can’t just go and pitch this. I have other stuff to do at the same time. So I was finding something that was relatively easy to do, a way to reuse Dylan’s animations that we already have. So I remember just going to one of our animators and going, “Hey, can you just throw me some of these animations? I have an idea.” --- Either way, the storyline was a consistent standout for Remedy’s playtesters, Grönroos and Burnic tell me. What they had to fine-tune — and very intentionally so — was the language and narrative of the physical space. In the final version of the mission, Dylan has to travel between three different research stations in the labyrinthine Underpass, an expanse of floating concrete islands, to search for the researchers. Ambiguity here was going to be a problem. “In the beginning, it was, like, identical stations, and we would more rely on the narrative content inside of stations to [tell you] what happened there,” Burnic says. In the final version, the stations share the same layout but are in visibly different states of disarray and disrepair. “We found a sort of language we could use. Station A was, ‘They were here for two weeks,’ station B [was], ‘They were here for three months,’ and I think the last one was the extreme one, which was like, ‘Oh, this was 10 years into this.’” The team used that concept as a guide to visually differentiate each station from the others. “And that came very much from a need,” Grönroos explains. “When we had people playtesting that mission before, they didn’t even know how many stations there were. Like, there were people who thought there’s one station, maybe there’s six stations, who knows, because they look so identical and the environment is not that easy to tell apart, either.” [Image: Concept art of the Underpass in all its brutalist glory. There were, aptly, a lot of iterations of this, and art was just part of it. One of the biggest changes was mechanical: You need the Reach ability, which allows Dylan to essentially grapple over long distances, to access the Underpass area to begin with. This wasn’t an explicit requirement early on, but it makes the floating islands of the Underpass much easier to navigate. And “it was the navigation issues that were keeping this mission down” during development, Grönroos says. But Dylan’s abilities presented their own problems. “If I remember correctly, we wanted to have certain beats, certain narrative moments, being represented to you first, and I think one of the biggest difficulties for me especially was that Dylan as a character is so powerful. The gaps he can close with his powers is quite insane, right? And it was so easy to break [the flow],” Burnic says. “I remember at some point kind of realizing that, however you twist and turn it, you can never really guarantee that a player sees this, and trying to guarantee it will be a bad design because it will be too hand-holdy,” he adds. “It was more like these narrative moments were pieces of the puzzle, almost. So it doesn’t matter which one you get to first, but hopefully the player will be able to put them together once they have all the pieces.” With a supremely powerful character like Dylan, Burnic says, “you need to lean into it and just design in a way where you can trust the player.” And with multiple timelines involved, seeing certain things out of the intended order wasn’t going to break the overall story of the mission. I certainly got turned around a few times in the Underpass and doubled back to look for collectibles I might’ve missed. But I didn’t struggle too much, and I understood the story Remedy was trying to tell — maybe not every single detail possible, but the most important beats, and definitely the unsettling, otherworldly mood it created. That was ultimately the “fragile balance” they had to strike, Grönroos says: trying “to have enough guidance that you understand what you are doing and where you’re supposed to be going” without holding the player’s hand. “It’s in the DNA of the whole game, really.”

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero's Kung Fu Punk Inspired 'Bold Musical Decisions to Match the Visuals'
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero Composer Caisheng Bo talked to IGN as the official game soundtrack is released for streaming and purchase.
articles.body:
Phantom Blade Zero composer Caisheng Bo is known as a pioneer in Chinese experimental music. As the soundtrack for the critically acclaimed action game gets announced for release today – a four-disc, 81-track audio adventure published by Milan Records – the music publisher shares the intriguing backstory of this soundtrack. "The musical story of Phantom Blade Zero began 18 years ago, when Caisheng Bo and Soulframe Liang—one in high school and the other in graduate school—were working on their indie game Rainblood 2: City of Flames, which would later evolve into the Phantom Blade franchise."

Bo, based in Beijing and a graduate of the University of Virginia in the US, spoke with IGN on the eve of the soundtrack's release.

IGN : From what I've seen of Phantom Blade Zero, the music very much ties in with some of the folklore and cultural themes explored in the game. Can you discuss how you sought to express this through music?

Bao : In traditional Chinese music, each instrument has developed a rigid set of associations—what it represents and how it should be used. I see this as a form of stereotyped expression. The erhu, a Chinese two-string bowed fiddle, is most often used to depict heroic action and the sorrow of personal endeavour. The pipa, a Chinese four-string lute, is associated with a feminine image and with danger on the battlefield. Anything outside these conventions may seem out of context.

This is the narrative I want to challenge in the music of Phantom Blade Zero. For each Chinese instrument, I set up a polarity between its traditional associations and a new set of meanings.

In Phantom Blade Zero, the erhu represents heroic action, as in the traditional idiom, but it also represents "manipulation"—a key image in which red threads descend from the sky, pulling enemies upward and controlling them. The pipa is tied not only to danger and the crisis lingering in the dark, but also to "discordance," an otherworldly realm where time stops and space distorts. The matouqin and Hoomai (throat singing), represent "mandate" and righteousness, while at the other pole they evoke megalophobia—the fear of vast objects. The xūn, a Chinese clay ocarina, is traditionally used to represent weeping, one of its signature playing techniques. In Phantom Blade Zero, the xun is also heard when Mu Tianmiao, a character of absolute authority, is present. These narrative polarities are among the design choices I made to enrich the game's story through music.

Alongside this innovative use of Chinese instruments, there are stuttering sound designs in the cutscenes, especially when Zuo Shang is plotting his scheme. As the story progresses, the stuttering sound grows louder and more present. This building stutter suggests his growing ambition—his uncontainable "Sha Qi" (killing intent).

By incorporating traditional Chinese instruments alongside modern musical genres and elements, I hope the music can cross cultural barriers, reach players' hearts, and offer them a truly distinct listening experience.

IGN : What other works of art inspired you for this project?

Bao : The music of the Phantom Blade series dates back almost 18 years to an indie game called Rainblood—that is where I began composing for this franchise. The music of Phantom Blade Zero is therefore built largely on what I have written over the years, though it has since developed into something uniquely its own. Most of the melodies have been carried over, but the stuttering sound design and the polarity between traditional and new meanings are entirely new.

IGN : How did your score evolve as you saw the game come together over the course of development?

Bao : Over the course of development, alongside a complete script, Soulframe would send me in-game footage of an area once they felt it was about 60% complete. They would play through the entire area—exploring hidden paths, defeating enemies, and finding treasures—just as a player would. As a result, I would regularly receive 4-hour-long video recordings for different areas of the game. I would then divide these areas into segments and plan the music for each one. In essence, I work as both music director and composer, which means I know where the music should start and what emotions it needs to capture. Once the team receives my music demo, they fine-tune the map, the combat, and the boss fights to match my music, ensuring that the game and the music sync perfectly with each other.

IGN : What are you hoping players take away from Phantom Blade Zero's soundtrack?

Bao : In vague terms, I would describe the ethnic Chinese music most listeners are familiar with as beautiful ancient villages or sacred temples—something that looks as if it has come straight out of an ink-wash painting, surrounded by tall mountains, beautiful waterfalls, and tall, sharp parasol trees. Because of Phantom Blade's unique concept of Kungfu Punk, I was able to make bold musical decisions to match the visuals. For Phantom Blade Zero, then, I want to introduce the modern side of Chinese music—think of Shanghai, a city of skyscrapers and flashy neon that is undeniably Chinese.

Beyond the question of the music's origins, I believe music is a universal language we all speak. I wanted to show the endless possibilities of combining Eastern ethnic elements with Western modern genres such as pop, trap, and metal—and how we can all appreciate the aesthetically astonishing results, regardless of cultural differences.

articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters Just Joined the Criterion Collection — And Now It’s 50% Off
articles.summary: KPop Demon Hunters officially joined the Criterion Collection earlier this week, and now the new release is 50% off.
articles.body:
KPop Demon Hunters officially joined the Criterion Collection earlier this week, and now the new release is already 50% off .

The quick discount has nothing to do with the movie’s popularity — The Criterion Collection just launched its November sale , which is essentially the distributor’s big Black Friday blowout. Through the end of November, every single Criterion release that has already come to market gets a 50% mark-down.

KPop Demon Hunters is the Collection's most recent release, having dropped this past Tuesday , and thus narrowly makes the cut-off to be a part of this year’s sale. It goes without saying these are the lowest prices yet on all three editions, which are still the only home entertainment release for the massive Netflix movie.

KPop Demon Hunters Is 50% Off in Criterion Collection Sale

KPop Demon Hunters (The Criterion Collection)

Pricing-wise, the 4K has dropped to $24.99 (from $49.95), the Blu-ray is down to $19.99 (from $39.99), and the DVD is $14.99 (down from $29.99). This 50% discount math applies to the entire Criterion Collection through Barnes & Noble, which offers relatively standard pricing across hundreds of DVD, Blu-ray, and 4K editions.

The timing likely isn't a coincidence, as Criterion often has a big release that just narrowly makes the sale cut-off. Ahead of the most recent July sale , it was the $400 Kubrick Collection, so at least this 'headliner,' if you will, is already more affordable.

As always, the Criterion edition has its own cover art. In this case, we get new artwork from Ami Thompson , who also worked on the film as a character designer.

The Criterion cover shows all three members of HUNTR/X using their personalized weapons in a joyful attack from the skies, recalling the opening 'Takedown' scene from the movie. The trio is accompanied by Derpy Tiger and Sussie Bird, depicted in front of mystical hints at the Honmoon.

The new edition also comes with a fresh slate of bonus features. While it unfortunately skips out on a commentary track, it does include a new making-of documentary, multiple video essays, and collectible postcards featuring original illustrations by artists who worked on the film, seen above.

New 4K digital master, approved by directors Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, with Dolby Atmos soundtrack

Full feature-length animatic, with a new introduction by Kang and Appelhans

Two video essays by filmmakers Taylor Ramos & Tony Zhou

English subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing and English descriptive audio

If you haven’t already seen KPop Demon Hunters, you must live under a very large rock. The movie was originally produced by Sony Pictures Animation, including some crossover with the Spider-Verse team, but dropped as a straight-to-streaming Netflix Original.

The generally low attention span of the streaming era was no match for the power of HUNTR/X, however, which proceeded to break multiple Netflix records and pick up a number of awards . Netflix has already promised to correct the record by giving the sequel a full theatrical release, but don’t expect to see it on the big screen until 2029 .

articles.title: Live-Action Stranger Things Prequel Gets First Teaser Trailer, 2028 Netflix Release Window
articles.summary: The live-action Stranger Things prequel series has its first teaser trailer and a 2028 release window, Netflix has announced.
articles.body:
The live-action Stranger Things prequel series has its first teaser trailer and a 2028 release window, Netflix has announced.

“Before Hawkins, there was Marion,” reads the tagline. The show is called Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, and it’s from The Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry.

Before Hawkins, there was Marion. Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure. A new series only on Netflix. 2028. — Netflix (@netflix) November 6, 2026

Before Hawkins, there was Marion. Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure. A new series only on Netflix. 2028.

The series is a prequel set in the 1950s, before Stranger Things and before the stage play Stranger Things: The First Shadow, which explores Henry Creel’s troubled past in Hawkins in 1959. Specifically, the teaser confirms April 19, 1955, in Marion, Nevada. We see a discarded bike outside a fenced off restricted area. "Use of deadly force authorized," reads the warning sign. The camera pans up to reveal a mystery facility lit up at night, before we move to focus on the sky above.

Golden Globe-winning director Joe Wright is set to direct the first three episodes of the new series, with production to take place in New Mexico. Expect a new era, setting and all-new characters, themes and mythology, Netflix added.

Jinny Howe, Netflix Head of Scripted Series, US & Canada: “Stranger Things has always belonged to the fans, and their passion made it a worldwide phenomenon. Today, on Stranger Things Day, we’re honored to partner again with Matt and Ross Duffer and Kate Trefry to give fans a new dimension of this universe to step into. Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure takes us to the 1950s with new heroes and all the heart, mystery, and spectacle of the original series. We’re proud to keep building this world with the Duffers, Kate, Shawn Levy, and Joe Wright, and we can’t wait for fans to see what’s next.”

Stranger Things Season 5 Finale Trailer Images

Co-Creators/Executive Producers Matt & Ross Duffer commented: “We’ve been dreaming of Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure for many years now, and to see it become a reality is surreal and exhilarating. We’re so grateful to our incredible team of collaborators: our showrunner Kate Trefry, who has been in the trenches with us since Season 2 and wrote Stranger Things: The First Shadow; and our director, Joe Wright, a brilliant artist whose work we’ve long admired. We can’t wait for you to see what they’re cooking up. It’s Stranger Things, but also thrillingly fresh, with a new setting, new heroes and villains, and new… actually, we’re not allowed to say any more. Now, on to casting. In the meantime -- watch the skies, nerds!”

Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure is far from the first Stranger Things spinoff we've seen from Netflix since the hit show came to an end in January, but it does promise to answer some burning questions left by the end of Season 5.

Warning! Spoilers for Stranger Things Season 5 Episode 8, The Rightside Up, follow:

In the Season 5 finale, we see Henry Creel / Vecna finally face his greatest fear: the traumatic memory of the day he was infected by the Mind Flayer and gained his powers. In this scene set inside Henry’s mind, we finally find out what was inside the briefcase that child Henry opens after bludgeoning its previous owner, an unnamed scientist, to death. Inside is a mysterious rock, which glows with an unknown energy before fusing with Henry. This, we understand, is how Henry became one with the Mind Flayer, and sets in motion all the events of Stranger Things that followed.

But what was this rock exactly, and how did it come to be in our world in the first place? An article on Netflix published as Stranger Things came to an end confirms the rock contains Mind Flayer particles, which then possess Henry. “Come find me,” the Mind Flayer beckons. And the dying scientist warns: “It will consume you.”

In a subsequent interview with Variety , Stranger Things co-creators Matt and Ross Duffer teased that the planned spinoff, which we now know to be Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, will explain all — and answer other plot threads left dangling.

“The spinoff is going to delve into that and explain that, and you’re going to understand it,” Matt Duffer said of the briefcase rock. “But it’s a completely different mythology. So it’s not a deep exploration of the Mind Flayer or anything like that. It’s very fresh and very new, but yes, it will answer some of the loose threads that are remaining.”

Stranger Things: The First Shadow Gallery

The briefcase scene is explained in vague terms by Stranger Things: The First Shadow, the canon play that acts as a prequel to the events of the Netflix show. We've run through the plot of the play already , but in summary, it confirms that Henry and the scientist are transported to what was then known as Dimension X. When Henry returns, he is much changed, and Dr. Brenner (Matthew Modine) eventually uses him as part of his experiments in Hawkins National Laboratory.

But even before then, the play tells us of a 1943 United States experiment to turn submarines invisible during World War 2. As part of this, they travel to Dimension X. Perhaps that's where the mysterious rock originally came from, and how it ended up in our world in the first place.

The Duffers previously described the spinoff as a “clean slate.” “Completely new characters, new town, new world, new mythology,” Matt Duffer said, adding: “No common characters.”

While you wait to find out more, check out the Duffer brothers explaining the ambiguity of Eleven’s ending .

articles.title: Snow Panic, an 8-Player 'SSX Meets Mario Kart' Skiing Game, Announced for PC
articles.summary: Developer KAFI has announced its next game, titled Snow Panic, which is an eight-player arcadey online skiing game that one of its developers describes as being like "SSX meets Mario Kart." It's in development for PC.
articles.body:
Developer KAFI has announced its next game, titled Snow Panic, which is an eight-player arcadey online skiing game that one of its developers describes as being like "SSX meets Mario Kart." It's in development for PC.

It's a downhill skiing game that will always feature competition; bots will fill in if you don't have enough human players in the match. And in that downhill race, the only rule is that the first one to reach the bottom wins. Bullets, rockets, and "suspiciously aggressive wildlife" will be amongst the obstacles you have to overcome as you ski towards the bottom. The developers mention airstrikes, mines, and a literal exploding goat as other hazards. Check out the announcement trailer below.

A clean run sounds like it's virtually impossible, by design. "Every hit is a full ragdoll crash, and every crash is somebody’s favorite clip," KAFI said. Expect six mountains to race on at launch, with more promised in post-release updates. Snow Panic also features proximity voice chat, because, as the team notes, "What’s the point of blowing up your friends if you can’t hear them scream as they fall into a ravine?"

There are 14 total weapons and items available at launch, and you'll be able to customize your skier's hair, outfits, and skis. You can wishlist Snow Panic on Steam if you're interested.

articles.title: The Expanse: Osiris Reborn Changes Actors for Its Male Protagonist and Updates Face Model
articles.summary: Actor Blythe Melin is now the voice of the male protagonist and his brother, J, in The Expanse: Osiris Reborn. This comes after fan reaction to the beta, which accused the voice work of being “flat” and “boring.”
articles.body:
Actor Blythe Melin is now the voice of the male protagonist and his brother, J, in The Expanse: Osiris Reborn . This comes after fan reaction to the beta, which accused the voice work of being “flat” and “boring.”

"While the voice actor for the male protagonist and J put in a lot of good work, they felt less expressive than we wanted," said the developer in a blog post earlier this year, before a replacement was announced. "Because of this, we are changing the voices of the male protagonist and J."

Melin is best known for his roles in animation, particularly in the DC comics universe, but the U.S.-based actor has also worked in video games doing mostly background NPC voices. As far as I can tell, developer Owlcat never announced who the previous actor was.

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn Updated Male Protagonist Face Screenshots

Funnily enough, this isn’t the only game inspired by Mass Effect to change the look of its protagonist based on fan feedback. Upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus also did a redesign of its male protagonist the other week.

For me, The Expanse: Osiris Reborn's new protagonist looks like Marco Inaros, the terrorist leader and commander of the Free Navy in The Expanse TV show. He liked flinging asteroids at Earth but was pretty chill about it. Anyway, the new face looks a lot like him — maybe it’s the hair in the example images.

That hair is up to you, of course. You’re able to customize how your protagonist looks, whether you choose the male or female version of the character. But like Commander Shepard has a canon look, so will this pair. Details on who voices the female protagonist and other cast members are coming at a later date.

"Voicing both the Captain and J has been an incredible joy and a unique challenge compared to the rest of my work voicing in video games over the years,” Blythe Melin said. “TWO, biologically related characters! It presented a difficult task in itself, because I find it very important to make sure neither character felt one-note-ey or too similar to the other.

“The more a character talks, especially in a multi-path dialogue route like for this game, the harder the task of making characters feel fleshed out while still having their own flavors and mannerisms. Playing twins has definitely been tricky, but there is somewhat of an easy divide that can be made between the Captain and J, in that one is an avatar for the player themselves, and the other is a pre-established co-character within the context of The Expanse. This allowed us to give J more of a solidified personality to work off of, with a lot of credit going to the writers and directors."

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn launches on PC, Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5 in spring 2027.

articles.title: Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 Stock Remains Depleted, Retailers Pivot to In-Store Drops
articles.summary: Finding a Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Switch 2 online remains nearly impossible, but major retailers are quietly restocking physical stores. Here is the latest stock breakdown.
articles.body:
Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition remains incredibly difficult to find online, with major retailers continuing to show the limited-edition console as sold out. However, that doesn't necessarily mean your chances of getting one are over.

With retailers increasingly shifting their remaining inventory towards physical stores (with several Ocarina of Time midnight launch events also featuring restocks for the special edition Switch 2 ), some fans may have better luck heading out to their local retailer than waiting for another online restock.

Nintendo Switch 2 - The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition

There are several reasons why retailers could be preferring to drop stock for in-store sales only, but an easy explanation would be simply that they are selling to real buyers, rather than aggressive bots set up by scalpers looking to sell the console at a profit.

That being said, retailers like Amazon and even Nintendo themselves are still occasionally going through restocks online, so it's still worth keeping an eye out every day in case you get lucky.

Along with the hype and success of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time arriving on Nintendo Switch 2 this week, demand for the anniversary hardware isn't exactly showing any signs of slowing down either.

After the summer reveal, preorders sold out almost immediately at retailers including Amazon, Walmart, Target, and Best Buy. Since then, online availability has remained extremely limited, with sporadic inventory appearing at Amazon and reports of Walmart orders being canceled due to stock shortages.

Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Console Images

Where to Check for Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 Stock

As I mentioned, Best Buy recently held special midnight openings at select locations for the Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2, with 40th anniversary consoles also available for select walk-in customers, rather than hosting any restocks online. Since then, there are no new signs of any further restocks occurring via the retailer's online store.

Target has also said it will have more stock in stores from November 5 onwards ( specifically stating it will also be in-store only in its weekly ad ), but it may also be worth keeping an eye online as well in case any turn up there as well.

GameStop and Walmart are the other retailers worth checking in person, although we'd recommend calling ahead to confirm whether it has any consoles available for walk-in purchases.

If you're still hoping to get your hands on the console, here are the retailer pages worth bookmarking for those still hoping to nab one online rather than in-person. Availability can change quickly, so it's worth checking each one rather than relying on a single retailer.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2)

The Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition includes a custom black-and-gold Switch 2 console, themed Joy-Con 2 controllers, and a matching dock featuring the iconic gold Triforce emblem.

It retains all the usual Switch 2 functionality, including TV, Tabletop, and Handheld modes, but doesn't include a copy of Ocarina of Time.

That means anyone buying the $519.99 console will need to pick up the game separately. Might seem obvious to some of you, but trust me, plenty will be confused that it doesn't.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is available for $69.99 at Amazon, with the new release bringing a rebuilt version of Nintendo's beloved 1998 adventure, complete with modernized controls, reworked dungeon puzzles, and expanded Hyrule environments.

Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller - The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition

It's also worth keeping an eye out for the matching Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 Pro Controller at most retailers as well, online and in store.

Like the console, the themed controller sold out shortly after preorders opened, and significant online restocks have been difficult to come by. Post launch-day inventory could offer another opportunity, although there are no guarantees of additional stock appearing going forward.

For now, I'd recommend checking your local stores before spending the day refreshing online listings.

The console may be difficult to find on a retailer's website, but that doesn't mean every last unit has disappeared from physical inventory. We'll continue monitoring Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Nintendo for further availability updates.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein in 4K Drops to a New Low Price in The Criterion Collection Sale
articles.body:
Guillermo del Toro's take on Frankenstein was a long time coming. The director had been open about his interest in the infamous monster since he was still knee-deep in the Hellboy franchise. When del Toro's Frankenstein finally came out, IGN gave the movie a glowing 9 out of 10 review .

You can watch it anytime on Netflix, but it's too good of a movie to stay on streaming forever. Thankfully, Frankenstein joined the Criterion Collection this past October. It's only been out for a couple of weeks, but thanks to Criterion's big November sale , you can already get Frankenstein's Criterion edition for 50% off from now until December 7.

articles.title: Adam Driver Talks About His Upcoming Turn as Mister Sinister in the X-Men Reboot
articles.summary: Adam Driver, best known for his turn as Kylo Ren in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, has discussed finally joining the MCU as X-Men villain Mister Sinister.
articles.body:
Adam Driver, best known for his turn as Kylo Ren in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, is finally going to be a part of the MCU after years of speculation. But instead of playing Magneto as rumors suggested , he landed the role of Mister Sinister in the upcoming X-Men reboot.

During a recent Jimmy Kimmel segment , Driver spoke briefly about the role and what drew him to it. “I was a big X-Men fan when I was a kid,” Driver said. “The TV show was right in my generation. It’s huge for me. Me and my cousin, Tony, he would be Sabretooth and I would be Wolverine — it’s a big deal.”

In the comics, Mister Sinister is the persona of Dr. Nathaniel Essex, a London biologist obsessed with engineering humanity into a perfect race of superhumans. When Kimmel mentioned the name of the supervillain on the segment, Driver couldn’t help but smile.

It’s a character he’s clearly excited about playing. As Kimmel pointed out on the show, Driver has been offered multiple roles by president of Marvel Studios Kevin Feige, but he’s turned them all down. He’s never wanted to be a part of the MCU, until now.

“I was a fan of the other things too, but this one felt like the right time, and it’s X-Men,” Driver said. Driver credited part of his willingness to take the role on working with director Jake Schreier, best known for the brilliant Netflix show Beef, and Marvel’s Thunderbolts.

“[Schreier's] idea for it, and Kevin Feige, it all came together, the script is really cool,” he said.

Wrapping things up, Kimmel asked why Driver is so careful when he says yes to a project. “A lot of people are going to watch it, and if it’s bad, people will see you being bad,” Driver replied. “Plus, I don’t want to mess it up. I’m a huge fan of X-Men.”

So far, Marvel Studios has confirmed a long list of names for its new MCU X-Men movie reboot, with its cast now including Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, and more.

articles.title: Yaga's Episode 4 Creates the Best Episode in the Series – Here's All the Chaos That Ensues
articles.summary: Episode 4 of Yaga pulls it all together to create the best episode in the series thus far.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Yaga Season 1, Episode 4. Episodes 1-4 are now streaming on AMC+ in the US and Crave in Canada, with new episodes releasing on Fridays at midnight PT.

The latest episode of Yaga pulls out all the stops to create the most incredible entry in the series so far. It’s aptly named “Dance With The Devil.”

We begin with Rapp having another vision, this time of Pam mixing together a drug or potion in a lab while wearing a white coat and the sinister mask from Episode 3 over her face. As she opens her coat, we see she’s not wearing a top and has the Triskelion symbol tattooed on her sternum. Rapp blinks and immediately is brought back to the reality of sitting on the other side of an interrogation room at the police department, while Carson is pressing Pam about her involvement with Logan the night he died.

As Pam insists she did nothing wrong, she does admit to loving Logan, and that she had an intimate relationship with him even after he started obsessing over Henry, who she deemed as being “such a fucking narcissist” for loving the attention he received from Logan.

Clark Backo utterly glows as Carson in this episode – the balance of sweet and intimidating in her intensity while interrogating Pam is mind-blowing. We really get to see her step fully into her role and it’s phenomenal.

While Carson is pressuring Pam to cave and give any information she’s withholding, she tricks her into admitting to having a threesome with Henry and Logan. In shots of the intimate scenes, we hear from Pam how obsessed Henry is with himself, saying it was his idea and “he didn’t like the idea of someone taking something that belonged to him,” referencing Logan. We see Pam and Logan eventually having sex, while Henry watches and pleasures himself in the corner, with Pam saying that Henry said it was like “watching a movie of himself” and being utterly entranced by Logan.

A theme that’s developing more prominently in every episode is men in this show consistently becoming more creepy and perverted. We have Rapp hitting on basically everyone, Logan with his disturbing tape recordings last episode, and in this episode, Officer Eckert, played by Patrick Gilmore, makes several side comments alluding to his attraction to Pam, who is a noticeably younger woman compared to himself – not to mention a suspect in a murder case, which just shows how unhinged his attraction is.

In search of more concrete evidence, Rapp and Carson head to the motel to have a chat with Angel about her tattoo. She confirms it is a Triskele (a variation of the Triskelion) with multiple potential meanings: death, life, and rebirth; fertility; the triple goddess; and past, present, and future.

We learn about a new character, Laney – an older Ukrainian woman who makes pottery and holds sabbats (guided meditations) in the woods. She creates “Villy,” the drug powder Rapp had taken the other night, which keeps showing up in places, including in Henry and Logan’s house. Angel very clearly states Villy is not a drug, but an “ethical organic dissociative tonic – a cure for every ailment” which we find out is made from chicken blood and human bone, and is taken during these sabbats for people to “manifest their dreams” and basically trip out.

Angel nonchalantly shares that, yes, Henry and Logan were both at these gatherings, piquing the interest of the buddy-cop duo, who fib to get more information out of her by any means necessary in order to find Laney.

As they drive to Laney’s house, the overhead drone shots where we see the car weaving through trees, and which are such a common motif in film and TV these days, take on a hauntingly beautiful feel which is enhanced by the entrancing score.

Carson and Rapp arrive at Laney’s house and, as they are peering around, they see someone fleeing from the premises. Unfortunately, they cannot identify who it is.

We see them searching carefully throughout Laney’s pottery studio and finding handmade jars that have the Triskele symbol on it – something Angel had said is “a mark of power.” Rapp comes across a worn-looking leather journal of Laney’s which is filled with sketches and recipes in Ukrainian – including what we now know to be the recipe for Villy. One of the sketches is of Baba Yaga’s house on chicken feet, and shockingly, another is of Henry wearing a flower crown while holding a chicken.

After digging for the whereabouts of Laney, they find out she’s at the hospital after suffering a fall, and are told she’s apparently delirious.

As Rapp and Carson arrive at the hospital, they find out Laney is, in fact, chaotically delirious, although it’s hard to tell how much of her character is deranged and how much she’s trying to deflect the questions Rapp is pressing her with, because she clearly knows things that are integral to finding Henry…

Rapp pushes her to share anything she knows about Henry, and as she sees a photo of him, she calls him a “bad dog” and says “he wants to dance with the devil.”

Carson steps into the hallway to answer a phone call from Eckert and finds out there was a video uploaded to Henry’s social media account. The utterly insane video shows Logan’s bedroom, complete with blood splattered around his window, as we saw last episode. The person recording shifts and moves the camera over the window ledge and we see Logan lying naked on the ground outside his bedroom window after he was allegedly murdered.

The person recording the video all of a sudden angles the camera onto a mirror in the room, seeing themselves in the reflection, wearing the creepy mask that appeared in Rapp’s visions more than once. They hold the shot on themselves for a few seconds before ending the video. Rapp and Carson now have a huge piece of evidence in Logan’s death that they need to decode.

We flip back to Rapp inside Laney’s hospital room, hearing him going back and forth asking her questions about Henry and “the devil” to get any type of answer. Laney keeps saying “wrong question!” over and over again like it’s a game. Then the music escalates, Laney’s heart rate spikes, the shots get tighter and faster going back and forth between them, and we finally hear Rapp yell “Who is the devil?!”... and everything stops.

Laney’s heart rate slows down as she grabs Rapp’s hand and kisses his palm saying, “Baba Yaga.” She cackles right before dropping back onto her bed as her heartrate flatlines. Laney’s dead.

Jessie Wade is Associate Director of Editorial Programming at IGN. You can find her watching the latest drama and fantasy shows, as well as getting lost in too many books. She's also low-key obsessed with cheesy rom-coms. In terms of gaming, you can find her playing the latest Pokemon, cozy indies, and Elder Scrolls Online.
